countries.visa: Golden Visa: property route CLOSED. Fund route from EUR 500K. NHR tax regime ended 2024.
countries.obstacles: Huge 10yr gains (+240%) suggest overvaluation risk. Property Golden Visa closed. NHR tax regime ended. 28% CGT and 25% rental tax are high. New DTA with Australia (signed 2023). Strong price-to-income (13.9). EUR eliminates local FX risk.
countries.profile: Market: Extraordinary 10yr growth (+240% nominal). NHR ended. Property Golden Visa closed. Market may be overvalued. Opportunity: Strong momentum. Good yields. EU membership. English widely spoken in Lisbon/Algarve. Risk: Potential overvaluation after +240% decade. Key tax incentives (NHR, GV) ended. 28% CGT, 25% rental tax. Entry: No restrictions. Well-regulated. Fiscal number required. Use local solicitor. Structure: Individual or Portuguese company. New DTA with Australia (signed 2023, pending). Consider timing of DTA entry into force. Timing: After 240% gains, correction risk is real. Wait for price consolidation or buy in less heated regions.
countries.rent_note: 25% on residential rentals
countries.cgt_note: 50% of the gain taxed at marginal rates 12.5-48%

countries.ownership: Foreigners can buy property with reciprocity. Australians generally can buy. Land purchase may require company.
countries.visa: No property-based visa. Standard permit routes.
countries.repatriation: Generally free. Managed float provides relative stability.
countries.obstacles: EU accession uncertain timeline. Declining population reduces demand. Limited transparency. Need to verify reciprocity for Australians. Low yields for the risk profile.
countries.profile: Market: Moderate. Belgrade-focused. EU accession uncertain. Quasi-EUR peg. Opportunity: Improving credit rating (BBB-). 15% CGT. Low purchase costs. Risk: Low yields. No DTA. Declining population. EU accession uncertain. Entry: Check reciprocity for Australians. Use local lawyer. Structure: Individual or Serbian d.o.o. No DTA. Reciprocity verification needed. Timing: Recent rating upgrade suggests improving fundamentals. Monitor EU progress.
countries.rent_note: 20% on real estate income
countries.cgt_note: 15%; the ten-year exemption is for residents only, so a foreign owner pays it

countries.rental_tax_text: 24% flat on gross (EU residents: 19% on net)
countries.estate_text: Yes (varies by autonomous community, up to 34%)
countries.ownership: No restrictions on foreign buyers. Full freehold. Very straightforward process.
countries.visa: Golden Visa CLOSED (April 2025). Non-lucrative visa or digital nomad visa alternatives.
countries.obstacles: Golden Visa closed. High purchase costs (10-13%). 24% WHT on gross rental (brutal for non-EU). Complex regional tax system. Strong tenant protections. DTA with Australia helps. EUR eliminates local FX risk.
countries.profile: Market: Strong recent growth (+10% real YoY). Golden Visa closed April 2025. Well-established foreign buyer market. Opportunity: Solid yields outside centre. Strong tourism supports short-term rentals. EUR-denominated. Risk: Golden Visa closed. 24% WHT on gross rental (non-EU buyers). Strong tenant protections. High purchase costs (10-13%). Entry: No restrictions. Well-regulated notarial system. NIE (tax ID) required first. Structure: Individual or Spanish SL company. SL may be more tax-efficient for non-EU investors. DTA with Australia. Timing: Strong price momentum but Golden Visa closure may cool foreign demand. Consider whether peak is approaching.
countries.rent_note: 24% on gross for non-EU residents, who cannot deduct costs
countries.cgt_note: 19% for non-residents without a permanent establishment

countries.cgt_text: Specific business tax (3.3%) or stamp duty (0.5%); income tax 5-35% on gain portion
countries.ownership: Foreigners cannot own land. Can own condo freehold (49% foreign quota per building). Leasehold land (30+30 yrs). Company structures possible but risky.
countries.visa: Thai Elite Visa (THB 650K-2M). No direct property-based residency.
countries.repatriation: Generally free with documentation of inward remittance.
countries.obstacles: No land ownership. High price-to-income (24). Low yields. 49% foreign condo quota can bind. Political instability history. DTA with Australia reduces WHT to 5%. Timezone close to Australia. Well-established expat property market.
countries.profile: Market: Well-established expat property market. Condos only (no land). Close timezone to Australia. Opportunity: Close timezone. Well-known market. DTA reduces WHT to 5%. Tourism supports short-term rental. Risk: No land ownership. Low yields. 49% foreign condo quota. Political instability history. Entry: Condos via foreign freehold quota. Must remit funds in foreign currency. Use reputable developer. Structure: Individual condo purchase. Company land ownership schemes exist but legally risky. DTA with Australia. Timing: Market has been flat. Tourism recovery supporting. Government discussing foreign land ownership reform.
countries.rent_note: not stated for non-residents on PwC
countries.cgt_note: not stated for non-residents on PwC

countries.ownership: Foreigners can buy freehold. Military zone restrictions. Cannot exceed 30 hectares nationally. Some reciprocity restrictions apply.
countries.visa: Yes - USD 400K property = direct citizenship (3yr hold)
countries.repatriation: Generally free but TRY weakness means FX conversion losses likely.
countries.obstacles: Extreme FX risk (TRY lost ~80% vs USD over 5 years). Very high inflation erodes real returns. Political/institutional risk. Citizenship route requires USD 400K which is above median. DTA with Australia helps on double taxation.
countries.profile: Market: Huge nominal gains but massive inflation and TRY collapse mean negative real returns. USD 400K citizenship route is the main foreign buyer driver. Opportunity: Citizenship-by-investment at USD 400K. Good rental yields. Large, diverse market. Risk: TRY lost ~80% vs USD over 5 years. 45% inflation. Political/institutional risk. Real returns likely negative. Entry: Straightforward for apartments. Military zone restrictions. Use certified translator and notary. Structure: Individual or Turkish LLC. DTA with Australia exists. Citizenship route bypasses many issues but requires USD 400K commitment. Timing: Inflation may be peaking (policy tightening underway). FX risk remains extreme for AUD-based investor.
countries.rent_note: not stated for non-residents on PwC
countries.cgt_note: real property gains not covered on PwC's income-determination page

countries.estate_text: No (Sharia inheritance rules may apply without DIFC will)
countries.ownership: Non-Arab foreigners can buy freehold in designated freehold zones only (major zones in Dubai, Abu Dhabi). 10yr Golden Visa with AED 2M+ property.
countries.visa: Yes - AED 750K property = 2yr visa; AED 2M = 10yr Golden Visa.
countries.repatriation: Free. No income tax. USD peg.
countries.obstacles: Restricted to freehold zones. High service charges. Market volatility (boom/bust cycles). Zero tax is hugely attractive. Strong Golden Visa pathway. Sharia inheritance risk (register DIFC will). Very liquid market. Close-ish timezone to Australia.
countries.profile: Market: Dynamic, volatile market. Zero tax. Golden Visa at AED 2M. World-class infrastructure. Opportunity: Zero personal tax. High yields. Golden Visa. Most liquid market in comparison. Very foreign-buyer friendly. Risk: Boom-bust cycles. Freehold zones only. Sharia inheritance (register DIFC will). Service charge inflation. Entry: Purchase in freehold zone (abundant in Dubai). Well-regulated. Fast process. Structure: Individual ownership is fine due to zero tax. Register DIFC will to override Sharia inheritance. Consider LTD for larger portfolios. Timing: Dubai market has recovered strongly post-COVID. New supply coming. Monitor supply/demand balance.

countries.cgt_note: no personal income tax

countries.estate_text: Yes (IHT: 40% above GBP 325K, no relief for non-doms from April 2025)
countries.ownership: No restrictions on foreign buyers. Full freehold (or long leasehold). 2% SDLT surcharge for non-residents.
countries.visa: Innovator Founder visa. No property-based golden visa.
countries.obstacles: 2% non-resident SDLT surcharge. 40% IHT (non-dom changes from April 2025 remove previous exemption). Strong tenant protections. Rental income taxed at marginal rates. DTA with Australia. Most liquid international market. English-speaking.
countries.profile: Market: Deep, liquid, transparent. 2% non-resident SDLT surcharge. Major non-dom IHT changes from April 2025. Opportunity: Most transparent market globally. Strong rule of law. English-speaking. DTA with Australia. Liquid. Risk: 40% IHT (non-dom exemption removed). 2% SDLT surcharge. Rental income at marginal rates. Strong tenant protections. Entry: No restrictions. Well-understood process. Use solicitor and tax advisor. Structure: CRITICAL - use corporate wrapper or trust to manage IHT exposure. Non-dom changes from April 2025 are significant. DTA with Australia. Timing: Prices declining slightly in real terms. Interest rate cuts may support. Market is mature and cyclical.
countries.rent_note: non-resident landlord scheme, net profits at income tax rates
countries.cgt_note: 24% for non-residents on UK residential property

countries.rental_tax_text: 30% WHT on gross OR elect net basis (10-37% graduated rates)
countries.cgt_text: FIRPTA: 15% WHT on gross; actual tax 0-20% + 3.8% NIIT on net gain
countries.estate_text: Yes (40% above USD 60K threshold for non-residents)
countries.ownership: No federal restrictions on foreign buyers. Some states have agricultural land limits. Full freehold.
countries.visa: EB-5 investor visa (USD 800K+ in targeted employment area). No property-specific visa.
countries.obstacles: High estate tax risk (40% above USD 60K for non-resident aliens - use LLC structure). FIRPTA withholding. Complex state-by-state tax. High property taxes in many states. DTA with Australia helps. Most liquid market globally. Consider LLC/corp structure.
countries.profile: Market: World's largest and most liquid property market. Huge regional variation. Strong fundamentals. Opportunity: Highest gross yields in comparison (10-11% Numbeo). Strong property rights. DTA with Australia. Extremely liquid. Risk: FIRPTA withholding. Estate tax risk (40% above USD 60K for non-resident aliens). State-level tax complexity. Entry: No restrictions. Process well-understood. Engage US tax advisor for structuring BEFORE purchase. Structure: CRITICAL - use LLC or corporation to avoid estate tax trap. US-Australia DTA helps. Consider state-level tax (no income tax in TX, FL, NV etc). Timing: Prices declining slightly in real terms. Interest rate cuts may support. Regional markets vary hugely.
